text: Chief Officer! The wind is increasing. And there's a dark cloud ahead.
Let me see… Yes, that's a squall. Rain and strong gusts. What's the barometer?
One thousand and six. It's falling.
Falling fast. That's the front. And the wind now?
The sea is rough. And there's a long swell from the north-west.
Good now. Five miles, maybe. But in the rain, much less.
Right. Close the door of the bridge wing and write it in the log: zero six thirty, wind north-west six, sea rough, barometer one thousand and six, falling.
Zero six thirty, wind north-west six…
Here comes the rain. Diego, keep a good lookout and report the visibility.
One mile. Standing orders: under three miles, call the Captain.
Captain, Chief Officer. We're in a squall. Visibility one mile, wind north-west seven.
Thank you, Tanya. I'm coming up.
